# H0 controls: synthetic residuals on the real design (prereg secs. 8, 3.5; the D2 grid)

*Generated by `scripts/generators/score_thiol_lolo_nested_tau.py --controls`; pre-registration `kinetic_core_between_lab_tau_h0_prereg.md` (v3). Every residual here is synthetic; no real residual was read. R = 1000 per configuration (P1 re-run at 4000), D2 grids 2000 per tau0, seed 20261101. Design noise: row sigma plus EX-056's saved engine class noise per fold (warm terms; reset terms where a fold has a reset arm), a published aggregate.*

**Hard criteria: P1 PASS, N1 PASS, T1 PASS, T1b PASS** -> no hard failure

- P3 (D1 interpretable): warm PASS, reset_where_leak_prone PASS
- P2 (test-inversion U >= tau in >= 93 %): PASS
- P5: largest P(UNSTABLE | tau = 0.8) = 0.627 -> the flag is uninformative (> 0.3): reported, changes nothing
- N2 PASS (flag only), N3 PASS (flag only), N5 PASS (failure: D2's multi-row-group fallback)
- D3a (size <= 0.10): PASS; sign-flip threshold 2/32; D3b power x = 0.054

## Choices (where the prereg is ambiguous; the reading taken)

1. Class noise for the controls' design: each row's s_i^2 = sigma_row^2 + the class noise saved in EX-056's fold record for the row's own laboratory (a published aggregate, not a residual), through fit_thiol_lolo.predictive_model. The warm set uses `models.engine_warm.terms`; the reset set uses `models.engine_reset.terms` where that fold has a reset arm (DFA, Jiangnan, Nestle) and the warm terms elsewhere, so the two sets differ in the design exactly as the real records do. The same s_i serve a laboratory's rows whether they are outer (fold L) or inner (a pair fit): the pair fits' training_terms do not exist yet.
2. Inner masks in the controls: an inner laboratory L''s rows are EX-056's paired rows of L' AND the rows both strict nulls (trained without L and L') can answer, the latter computed from row keys and species presence only (`null_answers`, no residual). In --score the mask is: finite under EVERY engine variant of the pair record AND both strict nulls (mirroring EX-056's paired definition, so one mask serves both sets and all three models).
3. Synthetic truth: one residual per row and replicate, the same in every record where the row appears (kappa = 0 outside the leak toy); the ABS and FIG level offsets are drawn independently per class with the same tau; FREE groups get an N(0, 1 dex) level. Every class shares the configuration's omega.
4. A laboratory enters omega(S) only if it holds at least one group with >= 2 rows; with none in S, omega(S) = 0 (flagged).
5. P1's six estimates are tau_ABS(all) and each of the five outer laboratories' nested tau_ABS(S). For Dalian and Reading (no ABS row of their own) tau_ABS(S) rests on 3 inner laboratories, for DFA, Jiangnan and Ochanomizu on 2. An estimate that takes the minimum-data fallback has no untruncated value and is listed, not checked.
6. The negative controls N1 - N3 are run at omega in {0, 0.3}, both sets, and must pass in every one of those configurations (the prereg names tau = 0 only).
7. P2's test inversion uses, per replicate, the f = 1 grid at the configuration's TRUE omega in place of the replicate's omega_hat(all) (recomputing a 31 x 2000 grid per replicate is out of budget); P2 is run at omega in {0, 0.3}. In --score the grid is drawn at the real omega_hat(all) of each set.
8. D2's bounds: U = the largest grid tau0 with P(tau_hat <= tau_obs | tau0) >= 0.05; L = the smallest tau0 with P(tau_hat >= tau_obs | tau0) >= 0.05 (the mirror); tau_hat is the TRUNCATED tau_ABS(all). U is computed per set at that set's tau_obs and omega_hat(all), and the ship rule reads the larger U, as it reads the larger tau. Grid edges (amendment A1): a U at the grid top is reported 'U >= 1.60' (and used as 1.60); a U that does not exist because tau_obs is below the 5 % quantile even at tau0 = 0.10 is reported 'U <= 0.10' and used as 0.10; an L at the grid bottom is reported 'L <= 0.10'; an L that does not exist (no grid tau0 qualifies) 'L: none'. Every two-set maximum is NaN-safe and order-free; an undefined tau_ABS(all) refuses D2 rather than reading as small.
9. UNSTABLE (sec. 3.7) compares the three drop-one estimates only (max t~ / min t~ > 2), and 'the other side of 0.8' is relative to the full tau_ABS(all). For D2 the flag counts if it fires in either set; it acts only if the controls' P(UNSTABLE) at tau = 0.8 is <= 0.3 in EVERY configuration (f in {0, 0.5, 1}, omega in {0, 0.3}, both sets): the largest is the gating number.
10. St (sec. 5): df = the number of inner laboratories holding the class (2 for most nests, 3 for tau(all)); arm (a)'s St uses df = the number of training laboratories holding the class in that fold. A class on the minimum-data fallback keeps a Gaussian level. The row marginal's CDF is computed by quadrature (Gauss-Hermite over the row error when the level scale >= the row SD, Gauss-Legendre over the t quantile otherwise; 64 nodes in the controls, 400 in --score); FREE rows keep the Gaussian rule.
11. S2 (the parameter term) is optional and is NOT implemented.
12. The relative branch (sec. 5.6) centres each group with >= 2 rows on its 1/s^2-weighted mean with the variance s_i^2 - 1/W + c_i omega^2(S) (the model's own nested omega); its LPD is the restricted Gaussian density with covariance diag(s^2 + omega^2) (invariant to the centring weights). A laboratory with no such group is left out of that comparison's mean.
13. Concentration check: the per-row contribution is (marginal log density of (b) engine - of (b) null) / n_L / K; the flag reads |sum of the top 5 % rows by |contribution|| / |sum of all| > 0.5 (the absolute-value share is reported beside it).
14. D3a and D3b simulate the engine and the null as two independent synthetic worlds on the same design (the engine's s_i), each with its own strict nested calibration; D3a passes if P(LPD criterion passes) <= 0.10 in both sets. 'D3 power = x' is P(the LPD criterion passes) at engine tau 0.8 vs null tau 1.2, the smaller of the two sets.
15. Exact bootstrap: the 90 % interval is (the smallest multiset mean whose cumulative multinomial weight reaches 0.05, the smallest whose cumulative weight reaches 0.95). The sign-flip p counts patterns whose mean is >= the observed mean minus 1e-12 (ties count).
16. D-all (sec. 5.8): every finite engine row of each fold. (a) is EX-056's predictive model on those rows; (b) uses the laboratory's strict nested omega / tau(S) for the five scorable laboratories, and tau(all) / omega(all) (S = the five scorable laboratories) for Nestle. Nestle is in EVERY EX-056 training set but its own fold, so each of those five fits was trained with Nestle: Nestle's (b) calibration carries the one-deep kind of leak (sec. 3.4), acceptable only because D-all is a diagnostic (corrected in amendment A1).
17. The jackknife (FRAGILE) drops one outer laboratory from the SCORING (D1 and D3 recomputed on 4 laboratories, 16 sign patterns, the same numeric threshold); the dropped laboratory stays an inner laboratory of the others' calibrations. Per dropped laboratory the two sets' jackknife verdicts are combined by the same precedence as the reported verdict; FRAGILE means that combined verdict differs from the reported combined verdict for some dropped laboratory (amendment A1). The per-set comparison is reported beside it.
18. Guard 4.1: relative difference |a - b| / max(|a|, |b|) (0 when equal); integer coverage counts must be equal. The curated-input check compares the provenance inputs under data/ with their EX-056 sha256. 'Read them at 7b1bc7cd' is implemented for data/keys/laboratories.yml (changed since EX-056 by appended laboratory groups only): its 7b1bc7cd version must hash as EX-056 recorded, and the fit table loaded with it must equal today's row for row; then today's file is used. Any other changed curated input fails the guard.
19. The ship-rule quantities tau_ABS(all), omega(all), tau_FIG(all) are computed on EX-056's paired rows of the five scorable laboratories.
20. The leak toy's FREE groups are perturbed in T1 too (D added to their level), with every class perturbed separately; T1b adds +3 dex to every residual of lab L in every synthetic record (fold rows, pair held rows, pair training rows) and divides L's synthetic data values by 10^3 (the nulls), then reruns the scoring step's calibration (training_terms, strict nulls, the estimator) for all three models and both sets.
21. --score refuses unless every pair record carries the same freeze commit, that commit exists and is an ancestor of HEAD, and this script, the pair runner, the controls record, the prereg, fit_thiol_lolo.py, fit_joint_deoxyosone_thiol.py, fit_deoxyosone_submodel.py, build_submodel_probe.py and src/kinetic_core/fitting.py are unchanged since it; a later change runs only with --amendment REASON, which is recorded (prereg sec. 7.5). Run once (amendment A1): --score refuses if the primary record exists, unless --amendment REASON is given; then it writes `..._amendment_<k>.{json,md}` (the next free k). Without a primary record, --amendment writes the primary record and stores the reason (a pre-scoring amendment).
22. Reproduction guards inside --score (amendment A1), before any nested number; a failure is INVALID (refusal): (i) training_terms(null_residuals(kind, train, train), train, n) reproduces each of the 12 saved EX-056 null terms (6 folds x 2 nulls) to a relative 1e-9; (ii) training_terms on the guard record's train_engine_raw['warm'] (row keys equal to split(data, ('reading_mottram',))'s training rows) reproduces Reading's saved models.engine_warm.terms to a relative 1e-9; (iii) engine guard 4.2(c) recomputed from the guard record against EX-056's Reading record: the warm cost to a relative 1e-3, the held-out raw residuals to 0.01 dex with the same finite mask. All three, and the freeze check, are recorded in the output.
23. One-deep mask (amendment A1): the one-deep sensitivity's inner blocks use the STRICT inner mask of sec. 3.2 (the rows finite under every variant of the pair (L, L') AND answered by both strict nulls), intersected with fold L''s paired rows where its residuals live, so |tau_onedeep - tau_strict| measures the leak and not a mask difference. The controls' T2 one-deep path is the same code (Nesting.calibrate), so T2 uses it too.
24. Missing inner laboratories (amendment A1): only a NON-CONVERGED pair fit (or impossible strict nesting) caps a set's verdict at INCONCLUSIVE. An inner laboratory whose rows are all removed by the strict masks leaves S and the minimum-data rule of sec. 2 applies, flagged; it does not cap the verdict.
25. Widths (amendment A1): the coverage table's 'median of lab medians' is the per-laboratory median 90 % width, then the median over the five laboratories (labelled so); beside it the pooled row median (every scored row of the five laboratories) and the lab-weighted mean width (the mean over laboratories of each laboratory's mean width).
26. Owner note on the relative branch (amendment A1): when D2 takes branch (i), the note fires unless the relative branch is shown better than BOTH nulls in EVERY set (the sets combined by precedence, so the worse set governs).
27. Labels and flags (amendment A1): verdict 4 reads 'CALIBRATED, NOT SHOWN BETTER THAN A NULL (D3 power = x, engine and null errors simulated independent)'. The controls' N2 / N3 / N5 outcomes are carried into the report as flags (N2: the nested tau_ABS(S) flagged; N3: the real tau_ABS flagged 'may be inflated by outliers'; N5: D2's multi-row-group fallback). The pair runner's unit tests passed at the freeze commit; the scorer cannot re-run them and says so.
28. Pair-record precondition (amendment A1): every one of the ten pair records must carry complete: true and the keys row_keys, held_engine_raw and train_engine_raw; otherwise --score refuses, naming the record and the key.

*Wall time 239.6 s.*
